name: Teutates

attributes.attribute: continental Celtic tribal god, name meaning ruler of the people
identified by the Romans with Mars and Mercury

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Teutates is a continental Celtic god. His alternate names are Toutatis, Totatis, and Teutate. His name appears to mean ruler of the people. It comes from a Celtic word for tribe. The name suggests an ancestral god. Dedications to Teutates appear most often in Gaul. They appear sometimes in Britain. They never appear in Ireland. Some texts connect him to the god Cocidius. Some treat him as an alternative form of that god. The Romans saw him as similar to their war god Mars. They also linked him to their trade god Mercury. The Roman writer Lucan said that Teutates received human sacrifice. He said victims were drowned to him on Samhain, the feast that starts winter.

okr.objective: Record Teutates as a continental Celtic tribal god.
key_results: States his name and worship across Gaul and Britain
Notes his link to Cocidius and the Roman Mars and Mercury
Records Lucan's report of human sacrifice at Samhain
